teardown.label: Real-world proof · Teardown #001
teardown.title: We ran Olmene on Olmene.
teardown.body: Before telling you what to fix, we pointed our own tool at our own homepage. It found five issues and scored us 89/100 — not a perfect score, because it doesn't know it's measuring us. We fixed everything it found the same day:
teardown.li1: Meta description trimmed from 181 to 155 characters
teardown.li2: Canonical URL added to every page
teardown.li5: This very section — its screenshot gives our image-alt check something to check
teardown.lesson: One finding taught us the most: after adding the JSON-LD, the check still failed — our own parser couldn't read @graph markup, the format most modern sites emit. So we fixed the instrument itself, redeployed, and re-measured. Every number on this page is real output, not a mockup.

teardown.afterLi2: Re-run any time — the checks never soften

faq.label: Questions
faq.title: Frequently asked, honestly answered.
faq.q1: Is this just ChatGPT with extra steps?
faq.a1: No. ChatGPT cannot see your website or change it. Olmene runs {n} deterministic checks on your real HTML, researches your market live with cited sources, and turns what it finds into pull requests you can review line by line.
faq.q2: Does Olmene need access to my code?
faq.a2: Only if you want fixes shipped. The free scan and the reports read your public site. To open pull requests, you install Olmene's GitHub app on one repository you choose. It can read that repository and open pull requests on it. Nothing else.
faq.a3: Olmene never merges anything. Every change arrives as a pull request on its own branch, with an explanation and undo steps, so you review it like a teammate's work. It never pushes to your main branch, and it skips any change it is not confident about.
faq.q4: Which sites and frameworks are supported?
faq.a4: Fixes ship for static HTML sites, Next.js (App Router) and Astro. Other frameworks will follow. Any public website can use the free scan and the full report, whatever it is built with.
faq.q5: What if my site is not on GitHub?
faq.a5: You can still run the free scan and buy the full cited report once. You get the same findings and a prioritized plan; you make the changes yourself.
faq.a6: Olmene re-checks your live site to confirm each merged fix is actually live. Paid plans keep re-checking those fixes every week and flag any that stop working, so nothing regresses silently.
faq.a7: Yes — one click in the customer portal. You keep access until the end of the period you paid for, and reports you already generated stay in your account forever. Failed analyses never count against your quota.

lp.s1.p: {{Account data:}} your email address and a user ID. If you choose Continue with Google, Google confirms who you are and shares your name, email address and profile picture with us under its own privacy policy; we never see your Google password or anything else in your Google account. {{Analysis data:}} the URL you submit, the optional context you add (product name, market, competitors, goal), the reports we generate for you, and technical job metadata. {{Repository data:}} only if you connect GitHub — the files Olmene reads in the repository you choose and the changes it proposes. {{Usage data:}} aggregate, non-identifying metrics like feature usage counts.
lp.s2.p: No passwords (you sign in with Google or an emailed link), no payment card data (handled entirely by Polar, our merchant of record), no third-party ad trackers, and no analytics cookies unless you accept them in the cookie banner.
lp.s3.p: Account and analysis data exist to provide the service: run your analyses, store your reports, and enforce your plan quota. We don't sell your data and we don't use it to train models — and the AI provider that writes your reports (Google Vertex AI) does not train on it either.
lp.s4.p: When you submit a URL, our crawler fetches that site's public pages — like a search engine would. We identify ourselves with a descriptive user agent and respect standard technical limits (timeout, page-size caps, few pages per site).
lp.s5.p: Your reports stay in your account for as long as it exists. If you delete your account, we delete your reports, jobs and account data within 30 days, except where retention is legally required.
lp.s6.p: Olmene is operated by Bytesphere_Dynamics (a trading name, not yet a registered company), which is responsible for your personal data. You can request a copy or deletion of your personal data at any time (GDPR/EU residents: this is your Art. 15/17 right). Contact us and we will comply within 30 days.
lp.s7.p: We use Google Analytics 4 — but only after you click {{Accept}} in the cookie banner. It shows once, the first time you visit, and you can accept or reject it. If you accept, Google sets {{_ga}} cookies to distinguish anonymous visitors (no personal profiles, and Google Analytics reports never include your IP address). If you reject, no Google Analytics code loads at all. You can change your choice anytime via {{Cookie preferences}} in the footer — rejecting again deletes the analytics cookies. Your Accept/Reject choice itself is stored in your browser's local storage, not on our servers.
lp.s8.p: Olmene relies on: Cloudflare (hosting), Supabase (accounts, database, background jobs), Google Cloud Vertex AI (the Gemini models that write reports and fix copy), Tavily (live web research), Brevo (sign-in emails), Polar (payments, merchant of record), GitHub (only when you connect a repository) and Google Analytics (only if you accept cookies). All of them process data only on our instructions.
lt.s1.p: Olmene (“we”) is operated by Bytesphere_Dynamics, a trading name that is not yet a registered company. It provides AI-generated marketing analysis reports based on public web data and the website URL you submit and, if you connect a repository, fixes proposed as pull requests. Reports are research aids, not professional consulting advice. You are responsible for verifying facts and figures before acting on them.
lt.s2.p: You need an account to run analyses. You are responsible for activity under your account and for providing a website URL you have the right to have analyzed. Don't use the service to crawl or probe sites you don't control with malicious intent.
lt.s3.p: Paid plans renew at the end of each billing period (monthly or yearly) until cancelled. A single report is a one-time purchase; its credit is valid for 90 days. Payments, taxes and invoices are handled by Polar (merchant of record). You can cancel any time — access continues until the end of the paid period. Failed analyses never count against your quota. Refunds for the current period are handled on a case-by-case basis; contact support.
lt.s4.p: Don't resell reports as your own consulting work without disclosure, don't attempt to overload the service, and don't use reports to make legal, financial or investment decisions.
lt.s5.p: Reports are generated by AI systems from public web data and may contain inaccuracies. Market estimates carry confidence levels and citations; technical checks are deterministic. We combine both, but ultimate judgment stays with you.
lt.s6.p: The service is provided {{as is.}} To the maximum extent permitted by law, our liability is limited to the amount you paid in the three months preceding a claim.
lt.s7.p: We may update these terms; material changes will be announced in-app. Continued use after changes take effect means acceptance.
lt.s8.p: If you connect a GitHub repository, Olmene's GitHub app can read that repository and open pull requests on it — nothing else. Every change is proposed on its own branch with an explanation; nothing reaches your main branch until you review and merge it, and you remain responsible for what you merge. Olmene skips changes it is not confident about. You can uninstall the app at any time in your GitHub settings.

meta.desc.security: Exactly what Olmene's GitHub app can and cannot do, how your code and data are handled, and who operates Olmene.
sec.h1: What happens when you connect GitHub, exactly.
sec.control: Olmene finds the problem and prepares the fix. Your team decides what gets merged.
sec.flow.title: The workflow
sec.flow.s2d: Deterministic checks and a cited report
sec.flow.s3d: Concrete edits, each with its evidence
sec.flow.s4d: On a new branch in your repository
sec.flow.s5d: Line by line, like a teammate's work

sec.gh.title: GitHub permissions
sec.gh.lede: Olmene connects through a GitHub App. GitHub shows you these exact permissions before you install it.
sec.gh.p1w: To read the files a fix touches (the file list and your homepage or layout files) and to commit the fix to a new branch.
sec.gh.p2w: To open the pull request and to see whether you merged or closed it.
sec.gh.p3w: Required by GitHub for every app: repository names and basic information.
sec.gh.none: Nothing else: no access to issues, Actions, workflows, secrets, settings, administration or your organization, and no webhooks.
sec.cap.title: What the app can and cannot do
sec.cap.c1: Read source code in the repositories you select
sec.cap.c1n: Only the files a fix needs: the file list and your homepage or layout files.
sec.cap.c2n: Only new branches named olmene/fix-…. It never moves or rewrites an existing branch.
sec.cap.c3n: One per fix run, with an explanation, the evidence and undo steps for every change.
sec.cap.c4n: Olmene's GitHub client cannot call GitHub's merge endpoint. You merge.
sec.cap.c5n: Every write goes to Olmene's own branch. A write to your default branch is refused before it is sent.
sec.cap.c6: Delete branches or repositories, or force-push
sec.cap.c6n: Delete and force-push requests are blocked in code, and the app has no administration permission.
sec.cap.c7: Access repositories you did not select
sec.cap.c7n: Each fix run is locked to one repository, and every request is checked against it.
sec.cap.c8: Deploy or change your production site
sec.cap.c8n: Changes reach production only when you merge and your own pipeline deploys.
sec.repo.title: You choose the repositories
sec.repo.p: When you install the app, GitHub lets you choose {{Only select repositories}}. Olmene can only see the repositories you pick, and each fix run works on the one you choose. You can change the selection or uninstall the app at any time in GitHub → Settings → Applications. Disconnecting in Olmene deletes the connection and checks that access has ended.
sec.prod.title: Production stays in your hands
sec.prod.p: Olmene never deploys and never merges. A fix reaches your live site only after your team reviews the pull request, merges it, and your existing deployment pipeline ships it. After that, Olmene reads your public website to confirm the fix is live; it needs no extra access for this.
sec.tokens.title: Credentials
sec.tokens.p: GitHub access tokens are created for each run, expire after one hour and are kept in memory only, never stored. The GitHub sign-in used when you connect is used once to confirm the installation belongs to you, then discarded. The app's own private key is stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM) with a key kept outside the database.
sec.safe.title: Safeguards
sec.safe.p: Every action is written to an audit log and to a receipt you can keep. Anything Olmene is not confident about is skipped, with the reason. An operator switch stops all repository writes at once; it is checked before every write.
sec.data.title: Data handling
sec.data.d1h: Used for sign-in (Google or an emailed link) and your plan.
sec.data.d2: Website URL, the context you add, your reports
sec.data.d2h: Used to run your analyses. Reports stay in your account.
sec.data.d3h: Read during a fix run, not stored. Olmene keeps only the proposed changes (the changed lines with three lines of context), the explanations, and SHA-256 fingerprints of each edited file before and after.
sec.data.d3k: With your fix runs, until you delete your account
sec.data.d4h: Used only to rate-limit free scans.
sec.data.d5h: Handled by Polar, the merchant of record. Olmene never sees card numbers.
sec.data.aiP: Reports and fix copy are written by Gemini models on Google Cloud Vertex AI, which does not train on customer data. The models receive public website content and research results. For a fix, they receive product facts from your report and the current page title, headline and image file names, not your repository files. Olmene does not use your data to train models either.
sec.data.delP: Ask us to delete your account and we delete your reports, fix runs and account data within 30 days, except where the law requires us to keep something. You can uninstall the GitHub app at any time without asking us.
